raw_market.question: Will Zven have the most kills at Worlds 2026?
raw_market.description:
This market will resolve according to which player records the most total kills across all official games played during the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026.

Every completed official game of the tournament counts (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count unless their kills appear in the official tournament statistics. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

If two or more players are tied for the most kills, this market will resolve to the tied player with the fewer total deaths across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied player with the more total assists. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the player whose listed in-game name comes first alphabetically.

If a player not listed in this market records the most kills, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official tournament player statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, official information from Riot Games (https://lolesports.com) and a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

raw_market.question: Will Ryze be the most played champion at Worlds 2026?
raw_market.description:
This market will resolve according to the champion that is played in the most official games during the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026.

A champion is "played" in a game when it is picked and played by either team in a completed official game of the tournament (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Bans do not count as plays. Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

In the case of a tie, this market will resolve to the tied champion with the higher win rate across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied champion with more bans across the tournament. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the champion whose name comes first alphabetically.

If a champion not listed in this market is the most played, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the tournament champion statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

A champion is "played" in a game when it is picked and played by either team in a completed official game of the tournament (Play-In, Swiss Stage, and Knockout Stage). Bans do not count as plays. Games that are remade, abandoned, or not completed do not count. Games awarded by forfeit without being played do not count.

In the case of a tie, this market will resolve to the tied champion with the higher win rate across the tournament. If a tie persists, this market will resolve to the tied champion with more bans across the tournament. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve to the champion whose name comes first alphabetically.

If a champion not listed in this market is the most played, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Worlds 2026 is canceled, or is postponed such that it has not concluded by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the tournament champion statistics on Leaguepedia (https://lol.fandom.com/wiki/2026_Season_World_Championship); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

raw_market.question: Will a Western team reach the Worlds 2026 Knockout Stage?
raw_market.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one Western team reaches the Knockout Stage of the 2026 League of Legends World Championship (Worlds 2026), currently scheduled for October 15 to November 14, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A Western team is a team that qualified for the tournament through the LEC (Europe / EMEA), the LCS (North America), or the CBLOL (Brazil). Teams that qualified through the LCK (South Korea), the LPL (China), or the LCP (Asia-Pacific) are not Western teams. A team that enters the Swiss Stage through the Play-In keeps the region it qualified through. A team is considered to have reached the Knockout Stage if it is officially confirmed as one of the eight teams advancing from the Swiss Stage to the Knockout Stage (quarterfinals).

If the Knockout Stage field is not determined by December 14, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or the tournament is canceled or postponed past that date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the tournament organizer, Riot Games, via the LoL Esports website (https://lolesports.com). However, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Liquipedia at https://liquipedia.net/leagueoflegends/World_Championship/2026) may also be used.
